Study uses CSF proteomics and SELDI-TOF MS, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (only MRI and SPECT/PET mentioned). Participants are described as FTD generally, not specifically clinically diagnosed bvFTD. Therefore inclusion criteria I1 and I2 are not met.

Study examines white matter hyperintensities and cortical thickness in cerebral small vessel disease patients, not clinically diagnosed bvFTD. Imaging focuses on cortical thickness measures (structural MRI), not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET. Therefore it does not meet the required sample (I2) or specified imaging modalities (I1).

Abstract is a narrative overview of genetic causes of dementia and does not report using VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET nor specify clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants. It is not clearly a systematic review/meta-analysis either. Insufficient information to confirm inclusion criteria from abstract alone, so include for full-text review.

Abstract explicitly states this is a review article ('In this review...'), so it meets exclusion criterion E1 (systematic review or meta-analysis). It also does not report original imaging data on bvFTD or use VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET in clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients.

Abstract mentions use of FDG-PET as part of patient workup (satisfies I1) and includes frontotemporal dementia patients, but does not specify behavioral variant (bvFTD). Insufficient detail to confirm bvFTD sample; include for full-text review.

Abstract explicitly identifies the article as a review (‘This review discusses…’). It is not an original imaging study of bvFTD using VBM, fMRI, or FDG‑PET. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E1 (systematic reviews or meta-analyses).

Abstract reports use of FDG-PET and structural MRI within FTD research, satisfying the imaging criterion (I1). However it does not specify clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD), so I2 is unclear. Include for full-text review to determine bvFTD sample.

Study uses FDG-PET (satisfies I1). The abstract reports frontotemporal dementia (FTD) patients but does not specify behavioral variant (bvFTD), so I2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract. No exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review to determine whether bvFTD patients were studied.

Although the study uses voxel-based morphometry (satisfies I1), participants are patients with amnestic MCI or early Alzheimer disease, not clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD. Thus it does not meet the required participant inclusion criterion (I2).

This study evaluates blood p-tau181 as a biomarker for Alzheimer’s disease, not behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD). It focuses on blood biomarkers and prediction of cognitive decline/hippocampal atrophy rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET imaging. It does not meet inclusion criteria I2 (bvFTD sample) nor I1 (specified imaging modalities). It is not a systematic review.

The abstract reports translation/validation of the Neuropsychiatric Inventory in dementia patients; it does not mention any imaging modality (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) nor specify inclusion of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients. It is not a review. Therefore it does not meet the inclusion criteria.

Abstract does not report using VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (only mentions MRI and SPECT/PET generally) and does not specify clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD patients (focuses on FTLD and dementia in ALS). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria I1 or I2.

Abstract clearly indicates this is a review article ('We reviewed studies'), i.e., a systematic/narrative review rather than original research. Excluded per E1 (systematic reviews or meta-analyses). The abstract does not present original bvFTD imaging data to satisfy inclusion criteria.

Abstract reports validation of a caregiver burden questionnaire and relationships with patient impairments; it does not mention any neuroimaging modality (VBM, fMRI, FDG‑PET) nor specifies inclusion of bvFTD patients. Therefore it is not relevant to the bvFTD imaging review.

Abstract is a general clinical overview/review of neuroimaging in dementia. It mentions modalities such as fMRI and FDG-PET but does not report an empirical study using VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET nor specify inclusion of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients. Insufficient information to determine eligibility from the abstract; include for full-text review.

The abstract describes Niemann-Pick disease type C and amyloid/tau deposition, not behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia. It does not mention VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET imaging nor clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants in the sample. Therefore it does not meet the review inclusion criteria.
This is a narrative review article of diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for tauopathies, not an original imaging study with primary bvFTD participants. Excluded as a review (E1).
Participants are clinically diagnosed Alzheimer’s disease patients, not bvFTD. Although FDG-PET was used (I1 satisfied), criterion I2 (bvFTD sample) is not met, so exclude.

The study sample comprises patients with early Alzheimer's disease (N=145), not clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients; thus it fails inclusion criterion I2. Imaging modality is MRI cortical thinning, but population mismatch is sufficient for exclusion.

This study reports hereditary diffuse leukoencephalopathy with spheroids (HDLS) due to a CSF1R mutation, not behavioral variant FTD. Imaging reported is MRI (structural), not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET. It is a case/family report, not a systematic review. Thus it does not meet inclusion criteria I1 or I2.
